question: Best verified index-calculus cost over matched Pollard rho (IC / rho), by date landed on main. Below 1 means index calculus is cheaper. The barrier is rho's own cost, 1.
unit_note: Each point is quoted from the frozen result it links, in that result's own unit (Valgrind Ir, S, counted operations, or isolated CPU time where marked). Only the direction against 1 is comparable across points; no value on this page is computed from another.

series.label: Elliptic curve, whole method, cold, one target
series.note: The repository's own definition of faster than rho (AGENTS.md section 2). Hollow markers were later shown to be measured against an unmatched rho and are kept as 'was'.

points.label: Tournament round 0007, five Koblitz cells
points.detail: 0.7376 of the worker rho's instructions, 95% 0.7066-0.7644. That rho named Frobenius classes by squaring; the control of 2026-09-23 showed it was not a matched reference.

points.label: Tournament round 0019, eight cells, strict win promoted
points.detail: 0.6751 [0.6298, 0.7265] of the worker rho's instructions on all eight cells; replicated by round 0020 at 0.6629. Same unmatched reference.

points.label: Control: rho given the IC arm's orbit naming
points.detail: The IC arm is above that rho at every cell measured, 1.19x (n59a0) to 2.88x (n43a1). Triple collector with counted sizing, five cells. Class accounting: what the ratios were counted against changed.

points.label: Tournament round 0024, matched rho, best cell n17a1
points.detail: Six of eight panel cells 0.61-0.82 of the matched rho; the strict gate fails at n23a1 (1.126); the whole twelve-cell panel reads 1.380 [0.847, 2.387]. Best cell plotted.

points.label: Tournament round 0025, lean rho, best cell n19a0
points.detail: The matched walk run in the IC arm's own single-word arithmetic. Above rho in instructions at every one of twelve cells: 1.36-2.56x on the panel, up to 13.7x past the crossing. The line was stopped on 2026-09-29.

points.label: Koblitz descent, one target cold, best size 2^38.0
points.detail: Ledger section 23: with the reusable set-up charged, the method is 4.9-31.6x slower than rho cold across six sizes 2^36.6-2^47.2; 2.0x at 2^38.0 where both arms pay a slow curve construction. Online only it is 8.8-17.5x faster (see the online series).

points.label: Orbit-disjoint cold CPU panel, closest cell n41/L1,024
points.detail: Six cells timing-eligible on reserved cores, every paired compact/rho CPU interval above one; the closest, n41/L1,024, reads 1.314 [1.288, 1.359] and would need 23.9% less CPU to match rho. Isolated CPU time, not a counted unit; S unset.

points.label: ecbench baseline, every candidate: best cell icv1-f2m17-tm101-00378d4e (r = 2^16)
points.detail: Every ic.pipeline configuration run cold through ecbench against the strong signed-Frobenius rho on the same targets, every phase charged in one unit: 4.30x at r = 2^16 (orbit base, Frobenius MITM m = 2), 129x at r = 2^21; on prime curves 7.70x at 18 bits rising to 40.5x at 24 bits. The reference is 18.5x its floor at this size because its fixed setup dominates, so the ratio flatters the candidate. No method changed; a baseline, not a round.

points.label: Pair claw of cryptanalysis#175, ported into ecbench: best cell icv1-f2m43-tm998717-e2e742b0 (r = 2^32.1)
points.detail: The four-point signed-Frobenius pair claw with a known-log orbit base (the PR's IC1 PDP4qtable LAnone candidate), run cold through ecbench against the strong signed-Frobenius rho on the same 48 Koblitz targets: 1.85x to 2.96x per curve at its cost-minimising table, 2.20x [1.90, 2.55] pooled; 32.6x [25.3, 41.0] at the PR's own n=83 shape. Flat in r, as a generic method must be. n = 83 itself is not measured.

series.label: Elliptic curve, 32 targets together (historical diagnostic)
series.note: Per target against batch rho on the same 32 targets, 39-bit Koblitz subgroup. Under the one-target rule this is a historical multi-target diagnostic.

points.label: Ledger section 19: reference matched to the batch
points.detail: Had read 1.17x against rho solving one target; against batch rho on the same 32 targets it is 6.5x, 6.4x priced by time on both sides.

points.label: Ledger section 20: every phase on the clock
points.detail: Re-priced on current main with the descent's 748,180-unit scan and the workflow's constructions charged: 12.5x. Best recipe swept at nine sizes reaches 4.9x at 2^39 and no lower.

points.label: Ledger section 21: constructions built once per base
points.detail: Whole pipeline 1.04-2.25x faster with every count unchanged; the row reads 4.3x.

points.label: Ledger section 22: descent fixed cost cut
points.detail: 1.35-1.39x at the small end in isolated runs; the row reads 3.6x. The closest any elliptic-curve pipeline gets end to end, and it is a batch figure.

series.label: Elliptic curve, online phase only (reusable set-up excluded)
series.note: Starts the clock after a reusable set-up. Not a cold result; the same set-up spent as a generic precomputation would speed rho up too.

points.label: Bounded autolab round 3, pair-table incumbent, six toy cells
points.detail: Paired IC/rho online cost 0.134x, descriptive 95% 0.125-0.144; the qualified rho online reference took 7.45x the incumbent's online time. 216/216 verified. Ledger section 23 (2026-10-01) reads 8.8-17.5x faster online at 2^36.6-2^47.2 on the Koblitz descent, and 4.9-31.6x slower once its set-up is charged.

series.label: Not an elliptic curve: hyperelliptic Jacobian, genus 4, toy size
series.note: p <= 251, N = 2^24, conservative accounting against a distinguished-point rho. The only end-to-end measurement below rho on the page; no deployed system is hyperelliptic.

points.label: Genus-4 crossover exponent
points.detail: 0.21 at N = 2^24 on the conservative accounting; fitted exponent -0.275 against rho.

points.label: Round seven: sparse solve priced, genus-3 claim withdrawn
points.detail: The solve became 5.1x cheaper and the linear algebra was priced; genus 4 reads 0.24 at N = 2^24 (was 0.21) with exponent -0.29 [-0.42, -0.16]; genus 3's exponent claim was withdrawn.

series.label: Weak elliptic class: cover and decomposition on E(F_p^6)
series.note: Joux-Vitse 2012 reproduced on a genus-3 GHS cover. The ratio falls as p^-1.92 and extrapolates to parity near 2^67 on this weak class (2^65 after F4 is stopped at the Bezout staircase, a 1.61x constant); the isogeny walk to reach it is unpriced.

points.label: Cover and decomposition, p = 1009 (subgroup 2^57.9), best of two seeds
points.detail: S/rho 8.1x and 10.2x at p = 1009, falling as p^-1.92 +/- 0.12 over five sizes; parity extrapolated near 2^67 (p* about 2,900-3,050), above the harness's 64-bit range. All 10 logarithms recovered.

points.label: Cover and decomposition, F4 stopped at the Bezout staircase, p = 1009 (subgroup 2^57.9), best of two seeds
points.detail: S/rho 5.1x and 6.3x at p = 1009 (8.1x and 10.2x before the stop): F4 stops once the leading monomials leave 64 standard monomials, the partial basis being a Groebner basis already; 1.61x on the test, the same relations from the same residuals, exponent -1.91 +/- 0.12 unchanged; parity extrapolated near 2^65 (p* about 2,300). Class: engineering.
